Header: Colletotrichum species ( C. capsici and C. gloeoesporioides )

Prevention: Use certified seeds and do not use seeds from infected fields.
Extract seeds from healthy pepper plants (obtain seeds from healthy fruits)
Effectively destroy old plant debris through burning immediately afer harvest
Transplant only healthy seedlings from nursery
Chilli and peppers should be rotated every 2 years with other non-host crops (e.g. maize, sorghum or groundnuts)
Ensure good drainage on the fields
Control weeds effectively because of wide host range of pathogen.
Monitoring: Monitor field after transplanting looking for early leaf spot lesions (dark brown to black spots).
Anthracnose can appear at any stage of development.
As plant grows, look for dieback in stem branches
Look also for black sunken lesions on matured fruits and fruit drop
Check for circular or angular sunken lesions with concentric rings on fruits
Use direct control measures at the first signs of disease.
Fungicides can be applied at first symptoms to reduce spread but preventative applications can also be used
Direct Control: Rogue and destroy early plants that show disease symptoms and burn to destroy

Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
